items.text: There is no single correct exam for every applicant.
Do not let a good score pull you into an unaffordable program.
Once the program requirement question is settled, or if a program genuinely accepts both, this is the honest fit test that most comparison articles skip in favour of generic advice.
You read fast and retain vocabulary without much effort
Text Completion and Sentence Equivalence questions are essentially vocabulary-in-context tests, and that skill is coachable but slow to build if it is not already there.

blocks.heading: What Counts As a Competitive Score

items.text: Score targets get repeated online without context constantly.

A combined Verbal + Quant score of roughly 320+ is generally seen as competitive for well-ranked engineering and computer science MS programs, with Quant carrying more weight for technical fields and a more balanced score mattering more for programs with a research or writing component.

Programs that accept GRE for MBA admissions typically look for a percentile-equivalent score comparable to their published average GMAT range, so check the school's GRE conversion guidance directly rather than assuming a fixed number applies everywhere.

blocks.heading: Four Questions Before You Commit Prep Months

items.text: The four questions narrows it down to what genuinely applies to your specific applications and timeline.
Before anything else, check the actual admissions page of every program on your shortlist for whether they require, prefer, or simply accept each exam.
Do not trust a forum thread or a coaching centre's claim about a program's policy.

blocks.heading: Mistakes to Avoid When Making This Decision

items.text: Acceptance of GRE for MBA admissions has expanded to the majority of business schools worldwide.
Some MS programs, particularly in the US, have dropped GRE requirements entirely, while others still require it strictly by department even within the same university.

A slightly easier prep experience is a weak trade if it produces a score the admissions committee weighs less confidently, especially at programs like ISB where GMAT submissions still dominate admitted batches.
